evidence.observation: "Its snapshot verdict equals the ordinary check verdict. The status is unchecked because the fixture supplies no derived claim." The evidence files independent-integrated.json and locked-integrated.json both record "run_status": "unchecked".
"The integrated close replays a supported check through accessor and worker, with single-evaluation rows and ordered explanations checked independently."

"Both hosts also evaluated an incorrect and a correct derived claim (exit 1 then 0)" is recorded only as claim_exit_codes [1, 0]; the text does not say those verdicts went through api.snapshot_verdict or the worker.

concerns.recommendation: Add a derived claim to the integrated fixture, or route the exit-1 and exit-0 claims through both the worker and api.snapshot_verdict. Record the resulting failed and passed statuses in each host transcript so the accessor and worker are shown agreeing on a non-vacuous verdict.
concerns.title: Integrated close shows accessor/worker agreement only for an unchecked status

evidence.observation: "Compatibility was exercised with the same wheel in two concrete Pydantic environments." No interpreter version or platform is named. Both host transcripts (evidence/PS4/*-host.json) record "python": "3.14.3", while pyproject.toml declares requires-python = ">=3.11".
"Record tested concrete versions, narrow supported ranges to evidence, keep lock exact."

concerns.recommendation: State in the close that both hosts ran CPython 3.14.3, name the OS and architecture, and say that 3.11–3.13 were not run. Alternatively, add a host on the lowest supported Python, or narrow requires-python to match the evidence.
concerns.title: Both installed hosts used one Python version; tested environment not disclosed

evidence.observation: "Other releases inside the declared interval have not individually been run." The interval itself is never stated. pyproject.toml declares "pydantic>=2.12.5,<2.14", which includes untested 2.13.0–2.13.3 and any future 2.13.x.
"The independent host used Pydantic 2.12.5 and the locked host used 2.13.4."

concerns.recommendation: Quote the declared interval in the close. Either justify an interval wider than the two tested points as consistent with 'narrow supported ranges to evidence', or record it as an explicit unverified claim.
concerns.title: Declared Pydantic interval is unstated and wider than the two tested versions

evidence.observation: "The final wheel SHA-256 is fd6c342ef66fd5ad79c42bd5f81738b82cae0488a1425809ccb7e22b73aee46e." The retained transcripts (evidence/PS4/*-host.json and *-integrated.json) record only "gnd": "0.5.2", so nothing ties that digest to the hosts that ran.

concerns.recommendation: Have installed_replay.py and integrated_replay.py record the installed wheel's SHA-256, or the dist RECORD hash, plus the commit, so each transcript names the exact artifact it exercised.
concerns.title: Final wheel digest is not recorded in the host transcripts

evidence.observation: PS2: "The broad run passed 937 tests with two deselected." PS4, which comes later: "The broad phase guard passed 912 tests with two deselected." PS3: "The final affected run passed 316 checks." No single full-suite run at the closing commit is reported.
"Milestone closure requires a replay across phases, a disposition for each issue and an inventory of unverified claims."

concerns.recommendation: Explain why the later broad selection has 25 fewer tests, or report one full-suite run at the final commit with its verbatim pytest summary. Say whether 'checks' in PS3 means pytest tests.
concerns.title: Broad test count drops from 937 to 912 between phases without explanation

evidence.observation: "count evaluations, expecting one"; "A relation that exceeds the row cap returns no partial rows. Cap requested relations and total returned rows; specify numerical bounds in PS2 and test equality and one extra."; "an equivalent renamed, reordered model"

"PS2 observes the computed extension during the same ordinary check. It distinguishes a complete empty relation from unavailable, protected and output-limited results." No evaluation count, numerical caps, cap-boundary result or renamed/reordered fixture is reported.

concerns.recommendation: In the close, state the observed evaluation count, the numerical relation and row caps, and the equality and cap+1 outcomes (no partial rows). Name the renamed/reordered fixture, or point to the PS2 record entries that hold these.
concerns.title: Close does not report PS2 single-evaluation count or cap boundary results

evidence.observation: "compares ordered and reversed targets with independent singletons. Per-target counters reset; exhaust the first of two and complete the second." and "Bound target count and per-target work at intake."

"resets walk budgets per target ... Changing the blocked relation invalidates the certificate." Nothing is said about reversed versus singleton equivalence, exhausting the first target and completing the second, intake bounds, or a fresh evaluation changing the outcome.

concerns.recommendation: Report the reversed-order and singleton comparison, the exhaust-then-complete result, the intake target and work bounds, and the fresh-evaluation outcome change alongside the stale-certificate rejection.
concerns.title: Close does not report PS3 order-independence, exhaustion and intake-bound evidence

evidence.observation: "Repeated worker checks surrounding an unsupported-version request have request IDs first, bad and again." and "replaced model bytes at the same path". In evidence/PS4/integrated_replay.py, the bad request is {**req, "version": 0}, which is a protocol failure, and the replacement is model.write_bytes(model.read_bytes() + b"\n"), which is semantically identical.
"force one invalid input, then evaluate a valid request" and "structured protocol and input failures"

concerns.recommendation: In the installed replay, add an input failure (malformed model or population) followed by a valid request. Make the same-path replacement change the semantics, for example by removing a fact, so a stale cached session would produce a visibly different verdict rather than just a different digest.
concerns.title: Installed worker replay covers only a protocol failure and a whitespace-only model replacement

evidence.observation: "Unknown and malformed reports have separate statuses and empty findings." and "Protect customer-mode callers from previously unredacted input."

"PS1 exposes api.snapshot_verdict for the supported snapshot wire versions ... The final focused run passed 119 tests." Separate unknown and malformed statuses, customer-mode protection and sensitive malformed inputs are not mentioned.

concerns.recommendation: Name the unknown and malformed statuses and the customer-mode and sensitive-malformed tests in the PS1 bullet, or cite where the PS1 record shows them.
concerns.title: Close omits PS1 unknown/malformed status split and customer-mode protection evidence

evidence.observation: "Draft r1, 2026-11-27 · awaiting plan review and owner decisions · auto=false. ... No panel was selected or run." The plan still says this, although revision 2 says it followed "six independent reviews".

"All five linked issues remain open pending merge to the default branch." There is no per-issue list of residual or unverified claims, for example #329's excluded includes and reference population dependencies.

concerns.recommendation: Update the plan status line to reflect revision 2. In close-delta, give each issue its own disposition with the unverified claims that apply to it, as §9 requires.
concerns.title: Stale plan status line and no per-issue inventory of unverified claims

response.summary: The close reports test runs for every phase and two installed hosts with matching evidence files, and the boundary note admits most limits. Four gaps remain. The integrated replay only shows the accessor and worker agreeing on an 'unchecked' status. Both hosts ran a single Python version (3.14.3) while the package declares >=3.11. The declared Pydantic interval is not stated, and pyproject includes untested 2.13.x releases despite amendment 4's 'narrow to evidence'. The final wheel digest is not recorded in the host transcripts. The results also do not map amendment 2/3/1 criteria (evaluation count, caps, exhaust-then-complete, redaction) to evidence, and the broad test count drops from 937 to 912 without explanation.

evidence.observation: The plan requires: "Replace model bytes at the same path, compare with a fresh session, kill and restart the worker, and prove isolation across requests."

The close reports that both hosts "replaced model bytes at the same path, killed the subprocess and verified that a newly started worker cold-loaded the replacement digest." The cited installed replay appends a newline to the model, leaving its meaning unchanged; the worker unit test uses the same kind of replacement. Digest and reuse checks cannot reveal a stale parsed model.

concerns.recommendation: In both installed hosts, change the model rule or facts at the same path so the expected evaluation changes. Compare the continuing worker’s result with a fresh session, then restart the worker and repeat the comparison.
concerns.title: Model invalidation lacks a changed-result replay

response.summary: The five issue dispositions and tested host versions are stated consistently. Worker model invalidation still needs a behavioral replay.

issues.message: reviewer invocation exited nonzero or required forced cleanup
reviewer response failed closed validation: invalid reviewer response: output contains no JSON object

evidence.observation: The close note states "The broad phase guard passed 912 tests with two deselected." with no timing qualifier, but the PS4 phase record (008-phase-PS4.md) reports the identical run as "pre-repair broad guards passed 912 tests with two deselected" and records that the initial independent review of 5b52e43f requested five changes; the only post-repair evidence the record lists is "Lifecycle tests passed (3), whole-tree lint passed". The broad regression pass therefore covers pre-repair bytes, not the final wheel fd6c342ef66fd5ad79c42bd5f81738b82cae0488a1425809ccb7e22b73aee46e, and the close note elides that distinction (unlike line 6, which at least separates PS2's broad run from its post-repair checks).

concerns.recommendation: Either rerun the broad phase guard against the final repaired bytes and report that result, or amend the close note to state explicitly that the 912-test broad guard predates the five review repairs and that post-repair coverage is the lifecycle suite plus the two-host integrated replay.
concerns.title: PS4 broad-guard pass predates the review repairs but is reported as unqualified final evidence

evidence.observation: The close note says "The numbered phase records identify the reviewed commits, covered inputs, test results and corrections." but nowhere discloses that the corrections themselves were not independently reviewed. The phase records state this plainly: PS1 "No later independent opinion on the repair." (002), PS2 "The repair at 4adbb93e has no second independent opinion." (004), PS3 "No independent review of the repair." (006), and PS4 records repairs of five requested changes with no re-review (008). Plan section 8 requires each phase to have an independent diff review; the independently reviewed bytes in every phase differ from the final accepted bytes.

concerns.recommendation: Surface the unreviewed-repair status in the close note and obtain an explicit owner disposition accepting it, or commission an independent review of the repair diffs before the milestone-close ruling.
concerns.title: Post-review repairs in all four phases lack any independent re-review and the close note does not surface this

evidence.observation: The reported PS3 evidence is "prepares a loaded snapshot once for an ordered batch, resets walk budgets per target and independently verifies a certificate for a covered, fully grounded asserted negative premise. Changing the blocked relation invalidates the certificate." Amendment 3 (plan revision 2, item 3) additionally ruled: "compares ordered and reversed targets with independent singletons", "exhaust the first of two and complete the second", and "Bound target count and per-target work at intake." Neither the close note nor the PS3 phase record (006) reports reversed-order comparison, first-target-exhaustion/second-target-completion, or intake-bound evidence, so per-target budget enforcement is asserted only via the reset claim.

concerns.recommendation: Record where the reversed-order, exhaust-first/complete-second and intake-bound tests live (phase record or test selection), or add that evidence, so each ruled PS3 scenario is traceable to a reported result.
concerns.title: Amendment 3's ruled ordering, exhaustion and intake-bound scenarios are absent from the reported PS3 evidence

evidence.observation: The close note claims "api.snapshot_verdict for the supported snapshot wire versions" without enumeration. Amendment 1 fixes that set as plain wires "7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 15-17 and reference wrappers 12/14", while the plan baseline (section 9) observed issue fixtures exercising only "raw schemas 7, 12 and 14", and the PS1 record (002) cites "plain, reference and admission wrappers, missing files and customer-mode projection" cases with no per-version list. Which of the eight plain versions carry test evidence is not identifiable from the recorded results.

concerns.recommendation: Enumerate the wire versions exercised by tests in the close note or phase record, or state explicitly that version coverage derives uniformly from interpreting the shipped report schema.
concerns.title: Broad wire-version support claim lacks per-version test enumeration

response.summary: All three digests match. The close artifacts are largely consistent with the five amendments and five issue dispositions: the delta accurately discloses the unexercised Pydantic releases inside pyproject's >=2.12.5,<2.14 interval, the open issues, worker locality and protocol boundaries; the two installed hosts (2.12.5 independent, 2.13.4 locked), final wheel fingerprint, integrated replay script and transcripts all exist; api.snapshot_verdict and allow_vacuous are present in src/gnd. Four concerns remain: the PS4 broad-guard pass is reported without its pre-repair qualifier; post-review repairs in every phase received no independent re-review, which the close note does not surface; amendment 3's ruled reversed-order, exhaustion and intake-bound scenarios are not evidenced in the reported PS3 results; and the wire-version support claim lacks per-version test enumeration.

evidence.observation: PS3 reports only: "prepares a loaded snapshot once for an ordered batch, resets walk budgets per target and independently verifies a certificate for a covered, fully grounded asserted negative premise. Changing the blocked relation invalidates the certificate. The final affected run passed 316 checks."

The ruling requires "compares ordered and reversed targets with independent singletons", "exhaust the first of two and complete the second", "Bound target count and per-target work at intake" and "Keep uncovered and exhausted distinct"; none of these cases appears in the reported results.

concerns.recommendation: Record in the close results the ordered-versus-reversed comparison with independent singletons, the exhaust-first/complete-second pair, the intake bounds on target count and per-target work, and the uncovered-versus-exhausted distinction, each tied to a named focused test; without them the PS3 amendment cannot be judged met from the close evidence.
concerns.title: PS3 close omits the ordered/reversed, exhaustion, intake-bound and uncovered-versus-exhausted evidence the ruling requires

evidence.observation: PS2 reports distinctions and counts only: "The broad run passed 937 tests with two deselected. Post-repair checks included 107 focused tests and 27 redaction tests." No numerical row-cap or requested-relation-cap value, and no at-cap or one-over-cap test, is stated anywhere in the close artifacts.
"Cap requested relations and total returned rows; specify numerical bounds in PS2 and test equality and one extra."

concerns.recommendation: State the concrete cap values for requested relations and total returned rows in the close artifacts and cite the focused tests exercising exactly-at-cap and one-over-cap inputs; a cap whose bounds and boundary tests are unrecorded is not demonstrably implemented.
concerns.title: PS2 close never states the numerical cap bounds or the equality/one-extra boundary tests

evidence.observation: "Multi-clause redaction follows all dependency clauses" and "27 redaction tests" are reported, but no reported check ties a protected-role case to the required ordering of projected disclosure before any data-dependent cap signal.
"Compute projected disclosure before data-dependent cap reporting for a protected role."

concerns.recommendation: Point to the specific protected-role test asserting the disclosure-eligibility decision precedes data-dependent cap reporting (e.g. an output-limit status that would otherwise leak cardinality), or add that test before closing.
concerns.title: Projected-disclosure-before-cap ordering for protected roles is not evidenced in the close

evidence.observation: "The integrated fixture in evidence/PS4/integrated_replay.py exercises all four phases in each installed host... The loaded batch reports derived then blocked... Its snapshot verdict equals the ordinary check verdict." The paragraph never states that the integrated run asserted a single evaluation producing the returned rows.
"The integrated close replays a supported check through accessor and worker, with single-evaluation rows and ordered explanations checked independently."

concerns.recommendation: Record the evaluation count observed in the integrated replay (expected one, per plan section 9) alongside the ordered-explanation result so both integrated assertions of amendment 5 are evidenced.
concerns.title: Integrated replay does not report the single-evaluation assertion required by amendment 5

evidence.observation: "Compatibility was exercised with the same wheel in two concrete Pydantic environments. Other releases inside the declared interval have not individually been run." The boundary document never states the declared interval itself, so the disclosed gap is not self-contained.

"Record tested concrete versions, narrow supported ranges to evidence, keep lock exact." Context from the repository: pyproject.toml line 27 declares "pydantic>=2.12.5,<2.14", whose endpoints match the tested 2.12.5 and 2.13.4 but whose interior releases remain unexercised.

concerns.recommendation: Restate the declared interval in the boundary document next to the two tested points (endpoints already anchor to evidence), or tighten the declaration if interior releases are not intended to be supported.
concerns.title: Declared Pydantic interval and its untested interior are not stated together anywhere in the close

evidence.observation: "PS1 exposes api.snapshot_verdict for the supported snapshot wire versions" — the supported set is not listed here.
"The Python verdict accessor interprets supported snapshot envelopes." — again without enumerating which envelope versions are in scope.
"PS1 supplies api.snapshot_verdict(report) over current plain snapshot wires 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 15–17 and reference wrappers 12/14."

concerns.recommendation: Carry the enumerated plain and wrapped version list from the amendment into the close results or the boundary document so the accessor's supported scope is auditable without reading source.
concerns.title: Close artifacts never enumerate which snapshot envelope versions are supported

response.summary: All three artifacts read with matching digests. The close is strongly disclosed (retained transcripts, wheel and model digests, concrete host versions, open-issue status, boundary doc), but several revision-2 rulings are not evidenced in the closing artifacts: PS2 never states the numerical cap bounds or the equality/one-extra tests, the projected-disclosure-before-cap ordering is uncited, PS3 omits the ordered/reversed comparison, exhaustion pair, intake bounds and uncovered-versus-exhausted distinction, the integrated replay does not report the single-evaluation assertion, and neither the supported envelope set nor the declared dependency interval is restated in the close.

criteria: Assess all five plan amendments and all five issue dispositions against the reported tests and two installed hosts. Identify any unsupported or inconsistent claims and scope issues by observable impact.
Evaluate disclosure, coverage, independent replay, per-target budgets, worker restart and exact supported environments. Distinguish a required correction from further coverage.
